primarySources.label: I. Primary Sources and Finding Aids

charterCompilations.label: Charter Compilations and Early Printed Authorities

entries.author: Vredius, Olivarius (Olivier de Wree)
entries.title: Genealogia Comitum Flandriae a Balduino Ferreo usque ad Philippum IV. Hisp. Regem (Pars Prima & Pars Secunda), with the Sigilla Comitum Flandriae
entries.publisher: Bruges: J.B. & Lucas Kerchovius, 1635–1643. Multiple imprints; the relevant volumes are detailed in the note.
entries.note: The single most important early-modern authority for this project, consulted across the several physical volumes that together make up Vredius's corpus on the Counts of Flanders (per-volume title-page dates verified 27 May 2026): (1) Pars Secunda, the 'Probationes' — standalone 1635 imprint plus the 1643 alt-edition bound with the combined 'a Balduino' set — is the load-bearing volume, reproducing verbatim the Ghent partition-court registers, charters, and tomb inscriptions of the comital bastard cohort. Tabula XVI covers the Louis I de Cressy bastards (pp. 267–275) and the Louis II de Male bastards (pp. 275–289), including the three Victor charters (pp. 285–287); Tabula XIX covers the 16th-century Praet generation (Lodewijk IV, Jossine van Praet, Jan II, pp. 387–388). The project's canonical distillation works from this volume, read at 300 DPI in April 2026. (2) Pars Prima (1642) supplies Vredius's narrative genealogy from Baldwin Iron-Arm to Philip IV, framing the Probationes. (3) Sigilla Comitum Flandriae (Bruges: J.B. Kerchovius, 1639) is the sigillographic companion reproducing the comital seals and diplomatic inscriptions, relevant to the heraldic and sigillographic context in which the surname emerges — it is the comital seal-book, not a source for bastard-line heraldry. FMG MedLands was consulted earlier as a tertiary pointer to these pages; that footnote crosswalk is kept in the project's research files.

entries.author: Espinoy, Philippe de l'
entries.title: Recherche des antiquitez et noblesse de Flandres
entries.publisher: Douai. Livre 2, Chap. XXXI.
entries.note: The principal authority for Victor's parentage and for the Praet territorial grants. Espinoy was a Flemish herald and his work is a foundational reference for Flemish noble genealogy, though he does not always cite his own sources. Quoted verbatim at many points by Vredius; this project consults Espinoy both directly (where the print is available via Gallica) and through the Vredius transmission.

entries.author: Bethune, J.B. de
entries.title: Epitaphes et monuments des eglises de la Flandre au XVIe siecle
entries.publisher: Bruges. Third part, p.356.
entries.note: Transcriptions of epitaphs from Flemish churches. The Oostborch epitaph for Jacqueline de Wilde and Josse van Vlaenderen is preserved here, providing the only direct evidence of Lodewyc van Vlaenderen's family through the physical burial record. The project also cites p. 233 (Elverdinge) for the epitaph evidence bearing on the identity of Robrecht van Vlaenderen's mother.

entries.author: Verschelde, Karel
entries.title: Geschiedenis van Middelburg in Vlaenderen
entries.publisher: Brugge: De Zuttere(-Van Kersschaver), 1867. ~272 pp. + plates, with a names/places index and a Bewysstukken document appendix.
entries.note: A Bruges local history of Middelburg-in-Flanders by the architect-historian Karel Verschelde (1842-1881). Its document appendix transcribes the 1441 Cadzand koopbrief as Bewysstukken N° 1 — the deed carrying the bare-with-honorific 'mher Victoors van Vlaenderen' attestation used in the project's register analysis of how recognized nobles of the cohort appear in fiscal and conveyancing records.

entries.author: Gailliard, J[ean-Jacques]
entries.title: Bruges et le Franc, ou leur magistrature et leur noblesse, avec des donnees historiques et genealogiques sur chaque famille
entries.publisher: Bruges: chez l'auteur J. Gailliard, rue de la Bride. Multi-volume series; the volume consulted on FamilySearch film 1116147 carries the date 1859.
entries.note: Genealogical and magisterial repertory of Bruges and the Brugse Vrije, transcribing tomb inscriptions and family records. Tome I pp. 257-261 is cited across the Praet dossier pages (Le Frison's two marriages p. 257; Jeanne de Flandre dite Drincham p. 258; the Aalter tombstone transcriptions p. 261, including Antoine van Vlaenderen gheseyt van Praet, d. 1522, at p. 260, photographed at NYPL May 2026). Vol. 3 p. 62 documents Jossine van Praet, dame de Moerkerke (d. 2 December 1546). Vols. 3-5 consulted via FamilySearch film; Tome I via NYPL photography.

entries.author: Pattou, Etienne
entries.title: Batards de Flandres
entries.publisher: Privately compiled genealogical register. Online edition.
entries.note: A compiled register of the documented illegitimate children of the Counts of Flanders. Tertiary compilation consulted as a pointer to the broader network of Louis de Male's bastard children; not cited as a fact-level authority. Pattou synthesises Espinoy, Vredius, and later Belgian heraldic literature.

entries.author: Anselme, Père (de Guibours)
entries.title: Histoire généalogique et chronologique de la maison royale de France, Tome I
entries.note: Four royal-bastard naming exempla page-verified (Marguerite de Valois p. 115; Diane légitimée de France p. 156; Louis-Auguste de Bourbon p. 192; Charles bâtard de Valois p. 207), seeding the francophone bastard-naming-precedent finding (Strongly Corroborated). Read 15 Jun 2026 from an OCR'd Gallica PDF (bpt6k76026j).

entries.author: Anselme, Père (de Guibours)
entries.title: Histoire généalogique et chronologique des grands officiers de la couronne, Tome II
entries.publisher: 3rd ed. Paris, 1726-1733.
entries.note: Grands-officiers-of-France genealogy; near-negative for the project overall, with one page-verified attestation: p. 1045, Marguerite de Flandres dite de Praet × Jean de Lannoy IV (issue Antoine de Lannoy, Grand Écuyer of Charles V) — a Praet-Vlaenderen-line daughter marrying into Lannoy. Tome II swept 13 Jun 2026. The comté-pairie-de-Flandre genealogy relevant to the cohort sits in a different, un-acquired tome; the 'le Haze' hits here are Jean de Chambly dit le Haze (a French family), not the Flemish de Haze.

entries.author: Hemricourt, Jacques de
entries.title: Miroir des nobles de Hesbaye (Jalheau augmented edition)
entries.publisher: Liège: Bassompierre, 1791.
entries.note: A Liège/Hesbaye nobility genealogy; project relevance centres on comital-Flanders bastards who married into Liège families. p. 71 fn.(d): Rufflar de Flandres, natural son of Louis I de Nevers (de Crécy), died at Crécy 26 Aug 1346 — the source MedLands cites for the Nevers bastard Ruflard. p. 206 fn.(b): Elisabeth de Flandre, dame de Somerghem, 'fille aînée naturelle' of Louis de Crécy, widow of Simon de Mirabello, remarried Arnoul de Montferant. Cross-flags the Three-Elisabeths disambiguation. Consulted 13 Jun 2026.

entries.author: Damhouder, Joos de (1507–1581)
entries.title: Manuscript notes underlying Praxis rerum civilium
entries.publisher: Bruges. Manuscript notes reflected in the 1567 printed Praxis rerum civilium and cited by name in Vredius's Probationes.
entries.note: Joos de Damhouder was a Bruges jurist whose manuscript notes on civil practice were a principal source for tomb readings and noble-family identifications in the Praet orbit. Vredius cites Damhouder by name for several Bruges-area tomb inscriptions relevant to the Van Vlaenderen-Praet line; this project consults Damhouder exclusively through the Vredius transmission.

entries.author: Gaillard, [Antoine]
entries.title: Manuscript collections: Ghent court partition records and tomb epitaphs
entries.publisher: Manuscript compilation; extracts preserved in Vredius's Probationes.
entries.note: Antoine Gaillard's manuscript collections are a key intermediary source for the Ghent court partition records and for tomb inscriptions quoted in Vredius's Probationes. Where Vredius attributes a passage to Gaillard, this project treats the attribution as the chain of custody for the underlying document and cites accordingly.

entries.author: Anon. (ed. Vorsterman, Willem)
entries.title: Excellente Cronike van Vlaenderen
entries.publisher: Antwerp: Willem Vorsterman, 1531. Large folio edition.
entries.note: Chronicle of the foresters and counts of Flanders, from Liederic de Buc (621 AD) to the late 15th century. Printed in 1531 as the first edition of a chronicle tradition preserved in seven related 15th-century manuscripts. The heraldic shields displayed on the Name page are from this chronicle tradition. Referenced for context on the world the Van Vlaenderen family inhabited.
entries.urlLabel: Free access (Utrecht University Repository — 1531 Vorsterman edition)

entries.author: Despars, Nicolaes
entries.title: Cronijcke van den lande ende graefscepe van Vlaenderen (405-1492)
entries.publisher: Ed. J. De Jonghe. Brugge, 1840-1842. 4 vols.
entries.note: The late-sixteenth-century Middle Dutch chronicle of Flanders by the Bruges patrician Nicolaes Despars, in the nineteenth-century De Jonghe edition. Cited site-wide: the narrative spine of the Maleani bastard-cohort attestations (the Vol. III master enumeration and the dated career entries for dHaze, Hector, Robrecht, Victor and their brothers) and of the project's Despars compendium. Pirenne's caution that the Cronijcke is 'hardly more than a translation' of Meyer's Annales is carried in the project's source-criticism; the two witnesses are read together rather than counted as independent.

entries.author: Meyer, Jacob (Iacobus Meyerus Baliolanus)
entries.title: Commentarii sive Annales rerum Flandricarum libri septendecim
entries.publisher: Antwerp: Joannes Steelsius, 1561. Posthumous expanded edition; the 1531 Annalium Flandricarum libri XVII was the first.
entries.note: The humanist Latin chronicle of Flanders by Jacob Meyer of Bailleul (1491-1552), in the canonical 1561 citation edition. Cited on dossier pages for the Latin-register attestations of the Maleani cohort — p. 200 ('Ludovicum qui & Aza'; the bastard-son roster including 'Hectorem Vorholtium', also at p. 163). Per Pirenne, the prior chronicle witness behind Despars's Cronijcke.

entries.author: de Smet, J.-J. (ed.)
entries.title: Recueil des chroniques de Flandre / Corpus Chronicorum Flandriae
entries.publisher: 4 vols. Brussels: Commission royale d'histoire / M. Hayez, 1837-1865.
entries.note: The nineteenth-century critical edition of the Flemish chronicle corpus. Tomes III-IV are cited on dossier pages: Tome III p. 278 for the 1382 Roosebeke host muster ('le Hase de Flandre') and Tome IV p. 311 for the December 1385 Peace of Tournai guarantor list ('Loys, bastard de Flandre, dict le Haze' — the French recension of the act independently attested in the Excellente Cronike). Tome I carries de Budt's Latin 'bastardo Flandriae' attestations of the cohort.

entries.author: Sanderus, Antonius
entries.title: Flandria Illustrata
entries.publisher: Cologne: C. ab Egmond et socios. 3 vols.
entries.note: A comprehensive illustrated gazetteer of Flemish towns, abbeys, and noble houses. Useful for identifying the geographic context of the parishes in the research area and for understanding the visual culture of 17th-century Flemish heraldry. This project consulted the 1735 Hague reprint of Tomus III (Carolus & Joannes-Baptista De Vos, 677 pp.), which bundles Flandria Illustrata with the Historia Comitum Flandriae Pars Prima and Pars Secunda; the methodology trail for the Oosteeklo-passage full-text search is documented in the project's research findings (Sanderus revalidation, April 2026).

entries.author: Sanderus, Antonius
entries.title: Historia Comitum Flandriae, Pars Prima: Flandria Ethnica — a primo consulatu Caj. Jul. Caesaris usque ad Clodovaeum primum Francorum regem Christianum, per DLIV annos
entries.publisher: In: Flandria illustrata, sive Provinciae ac Comitatus hujus descriptio, Tomus Tertius (1735 edition). Hagae-Comitum [The Hague] / Brussels: Carolus & Joannes-Baptista De Vos Fratres, MDCCXXXV.
entries.note: Sanderus's narrative history of the territory that became the County of Flanders, from Caesar's first consulate (59 BC) through the reign of Clovis I (d. 511). A distinct work from his better-known Flandria Illustrata (see sanderus-1641), though the two were bundled together in the 1735 Hague/Brussels expanded reissue, which is the edition consulted here. Pairs with Pars Secunda (Flandria Christiana) below. Useful for the pre-comital geographic and political framing of Flanders, and for Sanderus's handling of the legendary first-forester figure Liederic de Buc.

entries.author: Sanderus, Antonius
entries.title: Historia Comitum Flandriae, Pars Secunda: Flandria Christiana — a Clodoveo primo Francorum rege Christiano, usque ad annum DCCLXVII, Pipini Francorum Regis XVI
entries.publisher: In: Flandria illustrata, sive Provinciae ac Comitatus hujus descriptio, Tomus Tertius (1735 edition). Hagae-Comitum [The Hague] / Brussels: Carolus & Joannes-Baptista De Vos Fratres, MDCCXXXV.
entries.note: The continuation of Sanderus's narrative history of Flanders, running from Clovis I through the sixteenth regnal year of Pippin (767 AD). Covers the Merovingian and early Carolingian period of Flemish prehistory, ending just before the formal establishment of the hereditary county under Baldwin Iron-Arm in the 860s. Bundled with Pars Prima and with Flandria Illustrata in the 1735 Hague/Brussels Tomus Tertius.

entries.author: Froissart, Jean (ed. Kervyn de Lettenhove)
entries.title: Chroniques de Froissart
entries.publisher: Ed. Henri Kervyn de Lettenhove. Brussels: Académie Royale / Devaux, 1867-1877. 25 vols.
entries.note: Narrative chronicle for the Maleani-cohort generation; Froissart reports on the Flemish bastard cohort in passages other chronicles do not carry. The 1867-1877 Kervyn de Lettenhove edition is the canonical 19th-century recension. Vol. 1 in hand (IA: chroniquesrelati01kervuoft), acquired 27 May 2026; not yet read or source-noted. Sweep targets: cohort-relevant passages in Vols. 11-16 (1380s–1390s), Nicopolis 1396 in Vols. 15-16.

entries.author: De la Marche, Olivier (ed. Beaune & d'Arbaumont)
entries.title: Mémoires d'Olivier de la Marche
entries.publisher: Ed. Henri Beaune & J. d'Arbaumont. Paris: Société de l'Histoire de France, 1883-1888. 4 vols.
entries.note: Burgundian-court memoirist (c. 1426–1502), Charles the Bold's premier maître d'hôtel; canonical for Golden Fleece ceremonial detail. Vol. 3 in hand (IA: mmoiresdolivie03lamauoft), acquired 27 May 2026; not yet read or source-noted. Covers c. 1474–1488, the Burgundian crisis decade including the Karel II Langemark generation (d. 1491).

entries.author: Brugse Vrije, Staten van Goed
entries.title: Probate and guardianship records of Joos van Vlaenderen
entries.publisher: Rijksarchief Brugge (RAB), Brugse Vrije, Staten van Goed, Eerste Reeks, TBO 184, nrs. 21300 (1547), 21301, and 21302 (1549). Case reference 2026/0451.
entries.note: The earliest confirmed early modern documents naming a bearer of the Van Vlaenderen surname in the Meetjesland area. Bundle 21300 records Joos van Vlaenderen as testator, 1547; bundle 21302 records a guardianship proceeding, 1549; bundle 21301 is the intervening part of the same wardship series (the Honnelede wardship series, 1545-49, cited in the project's register analysis). Jacob's land described as adjacent to Phillip's — strong kinship indicator. Consulted in person, April 2026. Archival signature fully verified.

entries.author: Schepenbank van Belhoute (Assenede)
entries.title: Land-transfer record naming Jan van Vlaenderen and Aert Janse van Vlaenderen
entries.publisher: Rijksarchief Gent (RAG), BE-A0514, bundle 514_0545_00G_00550.
entries.note: A 1610 schepenbank document from Belhoute (Assenede) identifies Jan van Vlaenderen as son-in-law of the de Suttere family, and names Aert Janse van Vlaenderen as his son. Pushes the confirmed Assenede-area chain back one generation above the previously known Arnoldus 'Aert' active 1620s–1640s. Consulted and collaboratively transcribed in person, spring 2026.

entries.author: State Archives of Belgium (Rijksarchief / Archives de l'État)
entries.title: Parish and Civil Registers (Belgian State Archives)
entries.publisher: Rijksarchief / Archives de l'État (all Belgian provinces); Stadsarchief Gent; FamilySearch.
entries.note: The parish and civil-registration records held by the State Archives of Belgium, digitised and searchable through the AGATHA portal — national in coverage, not limited to East Flanders. These registers are the primary evidentiary basis for the documented lineage from Bassevelde through Boekhoute, Waarschoot, and Oostwinkel; the project's systematic searches (1580–1920) focused on approximately 45 East Flanders parishes, accessed via AGATHA and FamilySearch digitisation.

entries.author: Feys, Eusèbe & Nelis, Alois (eds.)
entries.title: Les cartulaires de la prévôté de Saint-Martin à Ypres, précédés d'une esquisse historique sur la prévôté
entries.publisher: Bruges: Imprimerie A. de Zuttere-Van Kersschaver, 1880–1884. 2 tomes (Tome I: charters 1102–1364, published 1880; Tome II: charters 1396–1543 plus historical esquisse and indices, published 1884).
entries.note: A 19th-century scholarly edition of the cartularies of the prévôté of Saint-Martin at Ypres, preserving the charter tradition of the institution from 1102 to 1543. Useful for the West Flanders side of the project: Ypres is the attestation locus of the 1376 Jacop van Vlaendre reference cited in Debrabandere's WFB2, and the cartulary indices contain numerous references to Ypres échevins and bourgeois whose names might feed the broader early-attestation picture.

entries.author: Van Vlaenderen American-line primary documents (1854–1913)
entries.title: Primary records for Charles Louis Van Vlaenderen (b. Bassevelde 1854, d. Covington KY 1913), emigrant ancestor of the American branch
entries.publisher: Belgian civil registers (Bassevelde, Oost-Vlaanderen) and American civil, court, and ecclesiastical records (Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky). Specific records consulted include: Bassevelde geboorteakte no. 52, 14 June 1854 (son of Engelbertus van Vlaenderen and Marie Catherine De Clerck); Allen County (Indiana) naturalization declaration, 5 October 1880; Lucas County (Ohio) Probate Court naturalization affidavit, 5 April 1884; Kenton County (Kentucky) death certificate no. 2793 and probate file, October 1913.
entries.note: The documentary chain anchoring the project's direct American line to the Bassevelde civil register. Charles Louis was born in Bassevelde (Oost-Vlaanderen) on 13 June 1854 and emigrated via Antwerp–New York in 1875 (per 1880 naturalization declaration; a later 1900 census entry gives 1877). The Bassevelde 1854 geboorteakte is the critical primary-source join between the European parish-record dossier and the American branch that prompted the Lions of Flanders project; all subsequent American records cohere with the Belgian origin despite orthographic drift (Van Vlaenderen, Van Vlanderen, Van Flandern, Van Vanderen, Van Flanderen) across U.S. records. Full evidence trail compiled in the project research record.

entries.author: Gilliodts-Van Severen, Louis
entries.title: Inventaire des archives de la ville de Bruges, Section Première: Inventaire des chartes
entries.note: The calendar of Bruges city charters from the 13th through the 15th centuries; all six tomes in hand as text-layer PDFs (series complete 17 Jun 2026), each separately source-noted. Load-bearing across multiple threads: Tome III p. 396 (1396–97) Victor 'den bastaerd van Vlaendre' at Nicopolis; Tome III p. 502 (1404–05) Victor's naval enterprise; Tome IV pp. 202–203 Catherine de Flandre fille bâtarde de Louis de Nevers; Tome V pp. 347–351 (Oosthove/Bailleul) 'dame Ysabel de Fland., vefve de feu mess. Loys de Bailleul'; Tome VI p. 443 (1499) Roland de Moerkerke office-bar 'obstant quil est illegitime.'

entries.author: Gilliodts-Van Severen, Louis
entries.title: Coutumes des pays et comté de Flandre. Quartier de Bruges. T. V: Coutumes de Sysseele, Thourout, Watervliet
entries.publisher: Brussels: F. Gobbaerts, 1892.
entries.note: Sysseele (= Sijsele) is the Praet-line territorial context. The appended Antiquitez de Watervliet states Watervliet and Moerkerke 'ghecoment ut het huus van Praet' and names Guy de Richebourg 'fratre comitis notho' alongside Jan de Moerkerke at Cadzand. Full PDF in hand and source-noted, 17 Jun 2026.

entries.author: Vanden Bussche, Émile
entries.title: Inventaire des archives de l'État à Bruges, Section Première: Franc de Bruges, Tome I — Chartes
entries.publisher: Bruges: Daveluy, 1881.
entries.note: Inventory of the State Archives at Bruges (Rijksarchief Brugge), Franc de Bruges fonds — a distinct repository and fonds from the Gilliodts Bruges city archives. Key entries: the 1442 Franc bastard office-bar ('nul bâtard ne pourra être ni bourgmestre ni échevin du Franc de Bruges'); Louis de Praet as imperial commissioner for the Franc (1546, 1548); Vrancke van Praet × Bladelin accord 1471. Full PDF in hand and source-noted, 17 Jun 2026.

findingAids.label: Archival Finding Aids and Heritage Inventories

entries.author: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy (FMG)
entries.title: MedLands: Flanders, Hainaut. v5.0
entries.publisher: Online reference. Compiled by Charles Cawley. Updated January 2025.
entries.note: FMG MedLands (compiled by Charles Cawley) serves two roles for the project. As a finding aid, it preserves verbatim excerpts from Vredius, Espinoy, Bethune, Buylaert, Père Anselme, and numerous manuscript sources, with numbered footnotes that let the original authority be identified; since April 2026 the dossiers cite those underlying authorities directly — principally the Vredius print, read April 2026 — and MedLands is acknowledged as the finding aid that pointed to them. As a methodological model, Cawley's practice of preserving verbatim primary-source quotations with numbered footnotes is the template for the project's evidentiary framework, including the distinction between 'directly attested,' 'strongly corroborated,' and 'hypothesis.' The FMG footnote crosswalk is kept in the project's research files, not on the site.

entries.author: Agentschap Onroerend Erfgoed
entries.title: Hoeve Hof van Wessegem. Erfgoedobject 33384
entries.publisher: Flemish government heritage inventory.
entries.note: The Flemish built heritage inventory entry for the Hof van Wessegem in Ursel. Provides the verbatim statement placing Victor van Vlaanderen and Lodewijk de Haze as lords of Wessegem before 1431, and noting the reversion to the comital domain. Directly attested. A regional heritage site (mijnplatteland.com, 'Ursel, een Meetjeslands dorp') offers an informal corroborating statement that Wessegem passed to Victor van Vlaanderen, 'another bastard son of Louis van Male,' in 1399 and that he often resided there; it is noted here only as low-authority corroboration of this inventory entry.

entries.author: Debrabandere, Frans
entries.title: Woordenboek van de familienamen in Belgie en Noord-Frankrijk (WFB2)
entries.publisher: Amsterdam/Antwerp: LJ Veen, 2003. ISBN 9020402072.
entries.note: The authoritative dictionary of Belgian family names. The Van Vlaenderen entry classifies the surname as a herkomstnaam (origin name) with PlN designation. Three attestations cited: 1280 Catharina de Flandria, 1376 Jacop van Vlaendre (Ypres, via BEELE), 1426 Jaquemaerde van Vlaendren (Kortrijk, via DEBR. 1958). CBG version is based on author's post-2003 manuscript with improvements — more current than the printed edition.

entries.author: Debrabandere, Frans
entries.title: Woordenboek van de Familienamen in Zeeland (WFZ)
entries.publisher: Naamkunde / Familiekunde Vlaanderen. Available as full PDF via naamkunde.net.
entries.note: Debrabandere's regional dictionary of family names in Zeeland. The (van) Vlaanderen entry yields a single Zeeland attestation: 1309-10 mijn here Robrecht van Vlaendren, Aardenburg (HAES. 169), identified by Debrabandere as Robert of Béthune, Count of Flanders (1305-1322), and therefore not a hereditary surname bearer. WFZ documents no hereditary van Vlaenderen surname bearers in Zeeland. This finding strengthens East Flanders as the surname's geographic core and constrains the Zeeland thread (Laureys Arentsz, Arent van Vlaenderen) to rest on other documentary sources. Searched and downloaded April 10, 2026.

entries.author: Debrabandere, Frans
entries.title: Persoonsnamen in Hulster Ambacht 1300-1400
entries.publisher: Handelingen van de Koninklijke Commissie voor Toponymie en Dialectologie (KCTD / HCTD), 2018, pp. 297-375. Companion register to the Gysseling-Debrabandere Persoonsnamen in de Vier Ambachten corpus; based on Debrabandere's excerpts of the Kortrijk-archive documents (Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekapittel) relating to Hulster Ambacht.
entries.note: A systematic register of personal names attested in the Hulster Ambacht jurisdiction (modern East Zeeuws-Vlaanderen) during the 14th century, derived from the Kortrijk Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekapittel archives. Lemma 233 (Half Vlaenderen, van) carries the etymology of the separate Half-Vlaenderen name-family cited on the Surname Origins page. Together with the Gysseling-Debrabandere 1999 Vier Ambachten register and Debrabandere's Woordenboek van de Familienamen, this is one of the primary Dutch-language prosopographical finding aids for tracking personal-name attestations in the Assenede-Boekhoute-Axel-Hulst arc during exactly the period when the project hypothesises hereditary surname use was crystallising in the region.

entries.author: Gysseling, Maurits (†) & Debrabandere, Frans
entries.title: Persoonsnamen in de Vier Ambachten, 14e en 15e eeuw
entries.publisher: Handelingen van de Koninklijke Commissie voor Toponymie en Dialectologie (KCTD / HCTD), vol. 71 (1999), pp. 491-588.
entries.note: Posthumous edition, prepared by Debrabandere, of Gysseling's (1919-1997) note-card corpus of personal names attested in the Vier Ambachten (Assenede, Boekhoute, Axel, Hulst) during the 14th and 15th centuries. The corpus was compiled chronologically from schepenbank and related records; Gysseling's original 600 note cards yielded approximately 3000 attestations of around 1000 distinct individuals (983 men, 13 women). This is the single most directly project-relevant name register in print: the Vier Ambachten geography is precisely where the Meetjesland Van Vlaenderen attestations cluster, and the time window (14th-15th c.) covers the period between the Victor cohort and the first Joos van Vlaenderen records of the 1540s. Searched April 2026: V-section entries 407 (Vlaminc) and 408 (Vlascopere, de) confirm no Van Vlaenderen entry at the critical alphabetical juncture, and zero Bucket 4 (hereditary surname-bearer) hits across all 3,000+ individual mentions covering Sint-Baafsabdij, Sint-Pietersabdij, Rijke Gasthuis, Nieuwenbosse, Sint-Janskerk, and Karthuizers Gent fonds for Zeeuws-Vlaanderen, c.1240-1500. Conclusion: Van Vlaenderen is not an indigenous Zeeuws-Vlaanderen surname formation; it arrives into Bassevelde/Assenede from elsewhere, most likely the Ghent hinterland, consistent with the 1568 Franciscus attestation.

entries.author: De Flou, Karel
entries.title: Woordenboek der Toponymie van Westelijk Vlaanderen, Vlaamsch Artesie, het Land van den Hoek, de graafschappen Guines en Boulogne, en een gedeelte van het graafschap Ponthieu
entries.publisher: 18 vols. Brugge: Drukk. A. Van Poelvoorde, 1914-1938.
entries.note: Karel De Flou's monumental toponymic lexicon of western Flanders and the Franco-Flemish zone, with dated attestations excerpted from primary records. The relevant volumes are cited on dossier pages — among them Vol. 12 col. 1153 (the 1456 'Ector van Veurhoute' fief entry at Balgerhoeke) and Vol. 16 col. 554 (fiscal-register attestations used in the project's register analysis).

entries.author: Beele, Wilfried
entries.title: Studie van de Ieperse persoonsnamen uit de stads- en baljuwsrekeningen 1250-1400
entries.publisher: Handzame: Uitgeverij Familia et Patria P.V.B.A., 1975. 2 vols (Deel 1: analytical study; Deel 2: Glossarium).
entries.note: The onomastic authority behind the 'BEELE' citations in Debrabandere's WFB2. Deel 2's numbered Glossarium dictionaries every person-name token in the surviving Ypres city and bailiff accounts. Lemma 2866 (VLAANDEREN, VAN, pp. 609-610) is the project's verbatim-captured core entry; the separate lemma 940 (halfvlaanderen) underpins the classification of Half-Vlaenderen as a distinct, ordinary toponymic name-family kept out of the comital-bastard corpus; lemma 2870 ((de)vlamink) is the parallel ethnonym family. Photo-bundle capture of the V-section and source apparatus verified at page-image level, June 2026.

entries.author: Debrabandere, Frans
entries.title: Het Woordenboek van de Familienamen in België en Noord-Frankrijk: Nog Corrigenda en Addenda
entries.note: A supplementary corrigenda-and-addenda note extending the 2003 Woordenboek van de Familienamen in België en Noord-Frankrijk (see debrabandere-wfb2). Debrabandere treats the main dictionary as a 'work in progress' and has issued periodic corrections; this note is the continuation of the 2007-2010 corrigenda series. Consulted alongside the main dictionary for up-to-date etymological and attestation information on Flemish-Dutch family names.

entries.author: De Zwarte Doos — Stadsarchief Gent (volunteer transcription project)
entries.title: Huwelijken Sint-Martinusparochie Gent, 1584–1796, gesorteerd op familienaam en voornaam van de echtgenoot
entries.publisher: Stadsarchief Gent (De Zwarte Doos). Available via the volunteer transcription project.
entries.note: Indexed transcription of marriage registers from the Sint-Martinus parish in Ghent, 1584–1796, sorted alphabetically by the groom's family and given name. Useful for targeted lookup of Van Vlaenderen / Vlaendren marriage records in Ghent during the period between the 1547 Brugse Vrije TBO 184 documents and the 18th-century parish registers already incorporated into the project's parish-record database. Not a substitute for the primary registers but an efficient finding aid for name-targeted queries.

entries.author: De Raadt, J.-Th.
entries.title: Sceaux armoriés des Pays-Bas et des pays avoisinants
entries.publisher: Brussels: Société belge de librairie / Oscar Schepens. T.I: 1897; T.II: 1900; T.III: 1900; T.IV (Supplément): 1901.
entries.note: A multi-volume sigillographic armorial of the seals of the Low Countries and neighbouring regions. Tomes I–IV all in hand as PDFs (added 12 Jun 2026). T.I pp. 454–456 (the 'Flandre (de)' headword) carries cohort-adjacent seals, including the Guy→Guy→Guy Assenede bastard line (1390–1424), 'S Loys de Flanders b' bailli de Waes (1453), and Lodewijk IV's 1517 Wessegem-mouvance holding (Fiefs No 10881); T.I p. 70 gives the brisure doctrine for comital bastards; T.I p. 398 validates Donche's 1312 Drincham citation; T.I p. 436 the 'Françoise van Vlaendre dite van Drincham' 1515 entry; T.IV p. 438 'Loeys dis li Haizes, bastars de Flandres, sires de Helverdinghe.' The FMG-relayed 1517 Knesselare charter reference (Lodewijk IV holding six fiefs of Wessegem), cited in the Praet and Gap dossiers, is now verifiable against the source in hand.

entries.author: Dehaisnes, C.; Finot, J.; Desplanque, A. (comps.)
entries.title: Inventaire sommaire des Archives départementales du Nord antérieures à 1790, Série B (Chambre des comptes de Lille)
entries.publisher: Lille: Archives départementales du Nord. Multiple volumes, 1865-1906.
entries.note: The published finding aid to the Archives départementales du Nord (ADN) at Lille — the repository behind the 'ADN B …' shelfmarks cited across the comital-bastard pages (e.g. ADN B 1273 stuk 10535, the 1372 Wessegem grant; ADN B 1604 fol. 184, the 1398 regrant to Victor; ADN B 43124, the Loys 'le Hase' cohort). The project reaches these folios via the published inventories and via secondary authorities (Lichtervelde 1935, Moelaert 1973/1978, Rogghé 1968); the underlying ADN folios have not yet been read directly.

groups.heading: A. Counts of Flanders — General History and Prosopography

entries.author: Nicholas, David
entries.title: Medieval Flanders
entries.publisher: Longman. London and New York.
entries.note: The standard English-language survey of Flemish medieval history. Chapter 12 covers the reign of Louis II de Male (1346-1384) in detail. Essential reading for non-specialist visitors to the site.

entries.author: Prevenier, Walter & Blockmans, Wim
entries.title: The Burgundian Netherlands
entries.publisher: Cambridge University Press.
entries.note: The definitive treatment of the transition from the Dampierre to Burgundian period (1384 onwards). Directly relevant to the project's central argument that the van Vlaenderen surname crystallised as a hereditary identifier at the moment of Dampierre succession.

entries.author: Buylaert, Frederik
entries.title: Eeuwen van Ambitie: De Vlaamse adel in de late middeleeuwen
entries.publisher: Brussels: Paleis der Academien.
entries.note: A sustained prosopographical treatment of the late-medieval Flemish nobility; the theoretical companion to the 2011 Repertorium. Methodology — using charter witness networks and property records to trace non-seigneurial lineages — is the model for the archival strategy in the Bridging the Gap section.

entries.author: Buylaert, Frederik
entries.title: Repertorium van de Vlaamse adel (ca. 1350 – ca. 1500)
entries.publisher: Ghent: Academia Press, 2011.
entries.note: The authoritative modern Flemish nobility prosopography for the late-medieval period. Pages 740–746 contain the dedicated Van Vlaenderen-Praet entry. Referenced throughout the Praet and Gap dossiers. A 56-image bundle covering pp. 736–759 (photographed by Constance at Yale, May 2026) is in hand and has been read for the pp. 740–746 Van Vlaenderen-Praet pivot entry and the p. 570 two-Van-Praet-families disambiguation; a full-volume scan is still pending, after which the remaining dossier citations will be re-audited against the primary text.

entries.author: Galbert of Bruges
entries.title: The Murder of Charles the Good, Count of Flanders
entries.publisher: Trans. James Bruce Ross. Columbia University Press, 1967.
entries.note: A 12th-century primary source included as contextual background. Galbert names Gervais de Praet as Chambellan de Bruges after the murder of Count Charles the Good in 1127.

entries.author: Vandermaesen, Maurice
entries.title: Le droit de livrée à la cour de Louis, comte de Flandre, en 1331
entries.publisher: In W. Blockmans, M. Boone & Th. de Hemptinne (eds.), Secretum Scriptorum: Liber Alumnorum Walter Prevenier. Leuven: Garant, 1999, pp. 279–306.
entries.note: An edition and analysis of the 1331 livery records (droit de livrée) of the court of Louis I, Count of Flanders, including the banneret roster that names Guy van Vlaenderen, lord of Richebourg. Cited on the Research page (notes_source_6) for the identification and dating of Guy of Richebourg; the project reaches it via Buylaert, Repertorium (2011), p. 738. Bears on the contested parentage of Guy of Richebourg within the comital house (Vandermaesen: a Nevers/de Crécy natural son; Despars: a bastard of Robert of Cassel).

entries.author: Warlop, E.
entries.title: The Flemish Nobility Before 1300
entries.publisher: Handzame: Familia et Patria, 1975-76. 4 vols.
entries.note: The foundational English-language prosopographical study of Flemish noble families. The alphabetic repertory of noble families in volumes 3–4 is an essential reference for tracing any lineage with pre-1300 roots in Flanders, including the van Praet family. Backlog acquisition target; not yet consulted directly.

entries.author: Blockmans, Wim & Prevenier, Walter
entries.title: The Promised Lands: The Low Countries Under Burgundian Rule, 1369-1530
entries.publisher: Philadelphia: University of Pennsylvania Press, 1999.
entries.note: The accessible single-volume companion to The Burgundian Netherlands (1986), organised thematically around state formation, social structure, and urban economy. Covers the Maleani-cohort period through the Burgundian transition. Backlog acquisition target; not yet consulted directly.

entries.author: Pirenne, Henri
entries.title: Histoire de Belgique, Vol. II: Du XIVe siècle à la mort de Charles le Téméraire
entries.publisher: Brussels: H. Lamertin, 1902.
entries.note: Foundational synthesis of the comital house's institutional history, covering the Maleani-cohort generation through the Burgundian transition; the framework subsequent Flemish historiography builds on. Vol. II in hand as PDF (IA: histoiredebelgiq02pireuoft), acquired 27 May 2026; not yet read or source-noted.

entries.author: Buylaert, Frederik
entries.title: Seigneurial Lordship and the State in the County of Flanders (c. 1350-1550)
entries.publisher: In: Graham-Goering, van der Meulen & Buylaert (eds.), Lordship and the Decentralised State in Late Medieval Europe, PBA 268. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2025. Pp. 90-106.
entries.note: Framework source for the seigneurie-as-nobility-transmission mechanism underpinning the Van Vlaenderen-Praet noble-status argument. Full read 8 Jun 2026; theoretical framework, zero surname attestations. Cites Speecke et al. 2023 (higher-seigneuries repertorium). PDF in hand and source-noted.

entries.author: Buylaert, Frederik & Adriaens, Margot
entries.title: Lordship, Capitalism, and the State in Flanders (c. 1250-1570)
entries.publisher: Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2025. ISBN 9780198945727. Open access.
entries.note: The master synthesis behind Buylaert's 2025 OUP chapter. Scoped read of Chs 4–6 plus framework, 8 Jun 2026. Load-bearing: corroborates le Frison's Woestijne/Praet grants (p. 271) and the Elverdinge-Vlamertinge 1434 reversion (p. 273); verbatim 1542 van Vlaenderen attestation (Lodewijk IV, pp. 179–80); names Robrecht 'Roeland van Vlaanderen, a Dampierre descendant' (p. 273); mentions Jacob × Catharina van Boetzelaer (pp. 227–28). PDF in hand and source-noted.

entries.author: Vandermaesen, Maurice
entries.title: Nikolaas Van den Steen, proost van O.-L.-Vrouw te Brugge en raadsheer van de graven van Vlaanderen
entries.publisher: Handelingen van het Genootschap voor Geschiedenis (HvGG), 117(1-2) (1980).
entries.note: Comital-council prosopography centred on Nikolaas Van den Steen, provost of Onze-Lieve-Vrouw at Bruges and councillor to the Counts of Flanders. Lower-priority context for the comital administrative milieu; not yet consulted directly.

entries.author: Rogghe, Paul
entries.title: Het Meetjesland: Bijdrage tot de Historische Geografie van Vlaanderen
entries.publisher: Handelingen van de Maatschappij voor Geschiedenis en Oudheidkunde te Gent, new series, vol. 18.
entries.note: A foundational regional history of the Meetjesland covering its administrative structure, parish organisation, and land tenure patterns. Essential background for interpreting the geographic clustering of the Van Vlaenderen surname.

entries.author: Lauwens, Patrik
entries.title: Verhalen uit de genealogie Van Praet
entries.publisher: Self-published (in eigen beheer), Berlaar, 2021. 116 pp. Available via www.laurentii.be.
entries.note: A genealogical narrative of the Van Praet family from its origins through the van Vlaenderen period, in fifty dated vignettes. Documents the 1373 sale of the Praet leengoed to Louis de Male. Useful for the Praet-Moerkerken line (distinct from the Van Vlaenderen-Praet line) and directly cited in the Praet dossiers; the author acknowledges thin source-keeping, so the project treats the collection as a pointer to canonical sources rather than as direct evidence.

entries.author: Verhoustraete, Arthur
entries.title: De heren van Praet te Oedelem
entries.publisher: Jaarboek 1967 (Jaarboek II), Heemkundige Kring Bos en Beverveld (Oedelem-Beernem-Sijsele), pp. 101-113.
entries.note: A chronological genealogy of the lords of the heerlijkheid van Praet at Oedelem and Aalter — the load-bearing local-scholarly source for the Aalter / Land van de Woestijne / Praet seigniorial geography. Cited on the Praet and Gap dossier pages, including the roster (#8) recording the three marriages of the bastard daughter Marguerite (Maldeghem, Hector van Voorhoute, Sohier de Gand).

entries.author: Serrure, C.P. (ed.)
entries.title: De geslachten Van Praet, Van Moerkercke, Van Ghistele, Van Halewijn, Vander Capelle, Vanden Berghe, Vander Gracht, Van Steelant en Vander Straten
entries.publisher: In: Vaderlandsch museum voor Nederduitsche letterkunde, oudheid en geschiedenis, Vijfde deel. Gent: H. Hoste, 1863, pp. 295-310.
entries.note: Nineteenth-century genealogical article in Constant Philippe Serrure's Vaderlandsch Museum on the interrelated Praet, Moerkercke, Ghistele and allied families. Cited on the Gap dossier for the Praet-Moerkercke cadet relations, including the 'van Praet gheseyt Moerckercke' parallel to the project's dual name-form analysis.

entries.author: Stichting Achiel De Vos (ed. J. Taeldeman, later M. Devos)
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600 (series)
entries.publisher: Aalter / Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. Twenty parish monographs to date under the successive scientific editorship of Prof. Johan Taeldeman and subsequently Prof. Magda Devos (UGent).
entries.note: A regional toponymic corpus comprising approximately 18,000 pre-1600 place-name attestations from RAG, ARA, SAG, and local archives across the Meetjesland and adjacent Ambachten. The series is freely downloadable as searchable OCR PDFs from meetjeslandseplaatsnamen.org/digitale-bronnen. The single most relevant published corpus for cadastral and landholder-derived toponymic evidence bearing on the Van Vlaenderen surname's Meetjesland footprint.

entries.author: Van de Woestijne, Paul (ed.); comp. Achiel De Vos & Luc Stockman
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600. Deel IV: De Keuren van Eeklo-Lembeke en Kaprijke. Band 1: Eeklo
entries.publisher: Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. 244 pp.
entries.note: Scholarly toponymic monograph for Eeklo, the adjacent parish to Bassevelde and Boekhoute. Full corpus scan of the chronological glossarium (13th c.–1626) conducted April 2026: zero Van Vlaenderen surname attestations at landholder or notable level. Consulted as part of the five-parish scan reported in the project's research findings.

entries.author: Devos, Magda
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600. Oostwinkel en Ronsele
entries.publisher: Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. 142 pp.
entries.note: Parish monograph for Oostwinkel-Ronsele by the series' chief editor. Oostwinkel is a core documented parish of the Van Vlaenderen line (Petrus Van Vlaenderen, 1634). Highest-priority acquisition target after Waarschoot.

entries.author: Vandeveire, Jozef
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600. Ursel
entries.publisher: Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. 344 pp.
entries.note: Parish monograph for Ursel — Victor van Vlaenderen's documented Heerlijkheid of Wessegem-Ursel. Acquisition-priority target: tests whether Victor's own name or his sons' names survive as landholder-derived parcel toponyms in the parish he actually held.

entries.author: Luyssaert, Jan
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600. Vinderhoute
entries.publisher: Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. 92 pp.
entries.note: Parish monograph for Vinderhoute, home of the Van Vlaenderensmolen and the Gerardus Van Vlaenderen (1759–1800) miller line. Acquisition-priority target to confirm or date the mill's naming relative to the 18th-century miller.

entries.author: De Wispelaere, Arno; Andries, Geert; Devos, Magda
entries.title: Meetjeslandse Toponiemen tot 1600. Waarschoot
entries.publisher: Landegem: Stichting Achiel De Vos. 337 pp.
entries.note: Parish monograph for Waarschoot, home parish of the documented 1568–1780 line (Jeremiah → Noe → Livinus → Petrus Raphael). The largest volume in the series and by a wide margin the highest-value acquisition target for Van Vlaenderen surname research. Most likely of all five priority volumes to contain direct surname attestations in the toponymic record.

entries.author: Stichting Achiel De Vos
entries.title: Bassevelde — pre-1600 toponymic glossarium
entries.publisher: Aalter: Stichting Achiel De Vos. Standalone chronological glossarium.
entries.note: Standalone pre-1600 chronological toponymic glossarium for Bassevelde (Ambacht Boekhoute), birthplace of Charles Louis Van Vlaenderen (1854) and terminal parish of the documented European line. Full scan April 2026: zero Van Vlaenderen surname attestations; no Vlaminc attestations either. Covers 1171–1630.

entries.author: Stichting Achiel De Vos
entries.title: Assenede — pre-1600 toponymic glossarium
entries.publisher: Aalter: Stichting Achiel De Vos. Standalone chronological glossarium.
entries.note: Standalone pre-1600 chronological toponymic glossarium for Assenede (Ambacht Assenede), site of the 1610 Jan van Vlaenderen of Belhoute schepenbank document. Full scan April 2026 yielded one suggestive positive: a "Victors Bunder" parcel ("moers gheheeten fictoors bundre", 1457, RAG-RG) fifteen years after Victor van Vlaenderen's documented death — flagged for RAG-RG follow-up.

entries.author: Stichting Achiel De Vos
entries.title: Oosteeklo — pre-1600 toponymic glossarium
entries.publisher: Aalter: Stichting Achiel De Vos. Standalone chronological glossarium.
entries.note: Standalone pre-1600 chronological toponymic glossarium for Oosteeklo (Ambacht Assenede), compiled principally from the RAG-AOE (Abbey of Oosteeklo) archive. Full scan April 2026: zero Van Vlaenderen surname attestations and no parcel-name derived from any "Isabella" figure — independent confirmation of the Oosteeklo foundress-claim finding. Covers 1228–1628.

entries.author: Augustyn, B. & Thoen, E.
entries.title: Van veen tot bos: Krachtlijnen van de landschapsevolutie van het Noordvlaamse Meetjesland van de 12e tot de 19e eeuw
entries.publisher: Historisch-Geografisch Tijdschrift, 1987.
entries.note: The key article on the landscape history of the northern Flemish Meetjesland from the 12th to the 19th century — precisely the geographic area of the Van Vlaenderen American-line research — documenting the transition from peat extraction to the sandy-loam landscape of the parish-record period. In Dutch. Backlog acquisition target; not yet consulted directly.

entries.author: Moelaert, R.
entries.title: Wessegem en zijn heren (and a related Loys 'le Hase' domain study)
entries.publisher: 'Wessegem en zijn heren', Appeltjes van het Meetjesland XXIV (1973), pp. 206–238; further article in Appeltjes van het Meetjesland (1978), pp. 6–56.
entries.note: Load-bearing local-scholarly study of the lordship of Wessegem and its holders, including Loys 'le Hase' and Victor van Vlaenderen. Cited on the Loys de Haze and Victor pages for the corrected 9 April 1372 dating of the Wessegem grant (against ADN B 1273 stuk 10535) and for Loys's second-generation children (the 1978 article places their mother at Loo, near Veurne). Reached via the published text; the underlying ADN folios not yet read directly. (1978 article title/volume to be confirmed.)

entries.author: Rogghé, Paul
entries.title: Article in Appeltjes van het Meetjesland, vol. 19 (1968)
entries.publisher: Appeltjes van het Meetjesland, vol. 19 (1968), pp. 252–253.
entries.note: Cited on the Loys de Haze and Louis Friese pages for Loys's second-generation children (p. 252 fns 70–71, citing the Desplanque and Dehaisnes-Finot ADN inventories) and for Marie van Ghistelle's prior marriage to Jan van Halewijn (Ghent civic record S.A.G. JJ3K 1424-25 fol. 73). Distinct from Rogghé's 1964 Meetjesland historical geography (see rogghe-1964). Reached via the published text; the underlying primary folios not yet read directly. (Article title within vol. 19 to be confirmed.)

groups.heading: C. Flemish Prosopography and Genealogical Methodology

entries.author: Dumolyn, Jan & Haemers, Jelle
entries.title: Patterns of Urban Rebellion in Medieval Flanders
entries.publisher: Journal of Medieval History, 31(4), 369-393.
entries.note: Provides context for the social position of comital bastards — including why the sons of Victor and Louis Friese would have occupied an ambiguous status between nobility and commoner, and why their surnames might have been preserved through patronage networks.

groups.heading: D. Genetic Genealogy and Y-DNA Methodology

entries.author: King, Turi E. & Jobling, Mark A.
entries.title: Founders, Drift, and Infidelity: The Relationship between Y Chromosome Diversity and Patrilineal Surnames
entries.publisher: Molecular Biology and Evolution, 26(5), 1093-1102.
entries.note: A landmark study establishing the theoretical basis for using Y-DNA to test the hypothesis that a surname derives from a small number of founding males. The methodology is directly applicable to the Van Vlaenderen project.

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., Vanderheyden, N., Van Geystelen, A., van Oven, M., Kayser, M., & Decorte, R.
entries.title: Increasing phylogenetic resolution still informative for Y chromosomal studies on West-European populations
entries.publisher: Forensic Science International: Genetics, 9, 179–185. doi:10.1016/j.fsigen.2013.04.002.
entries.note: The Flanders-specific study underlying the KU Leuven Y-chromosomal reference database for the Low Countries. More than 1000 Flemish Y chromosomes were genotyped at the finest resolution of the then-current AMY-tree, establishing the regional sub-haplogroup frequency profile that later studies (including Larmuseau 2014) compare against. The most directly relevant reference for situating R-U106 / R-FT1573 results from Pieter van Vlaanderen's Big Y-700 testing within the Flemish population frame. (Epub 2013-05-14; print citation 2014 but DOI and epub year are 2013.)

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., Vanoverbeke, J., Van Geystelen, A., Defraene, G., Vanderheyden, N., Matthys, K., Wenseleers, T., & Decorte, R.
entries.title: Low historical rates of cuckoldry in a Western European human population traced by Y-chromosome and genealogical data
entries.publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences, 280(1772), 20132400. doi:10.1098/rspb.2013.2400.
entries.note: The first large-scale, unbiased genetic study of historical extra-pair paternity (EPP) rates in a Western European population, combining Y-chromosomal data from contemporary Flemish men with genealogical and surname records to estimate the historical non-paternity event rate. The study finds an EPP rate of approximately one percent per generation across roughly four centuries in Flanders, substantially lower than the eight to thirty percent per generation reported in some behavioural studies. Methodologically and geographically the most directly relevant prior work for the Van Vlaenderen project: it establishes the empirical baseline against which any apparent surname-paternity discrepancy in the Flemish Y-DNA record must be assessed. The roughly 1%-per-generation NPE rate cited on the project's DNA page derives from this study.

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., Delorme, P., Germain, P., Vanderheyden, N., Gilissen, A., Van Geystelen, A., Cassiman, J.-J., & Decorte, R.
entries.title: Genetic genealogy reveals true Y haplogroup of House of Bourbon contradicting recent identification of the presumed remains of two French Kings
entries.publisher: European Journal of Human Genetics, 22(6), 681–687. doi:10.1038/ejhg.2013.211.
entries.note: The methodological touchstone for this project's Y-DNA work. Larmuseau and co-authors collected samples from three living documented Bourbon paternal descendants and demonstrated that the reconstructed 'true' Bourbon Y-chromosomal variant (R-Z381*, a subclade of R-U106) is incompatible with the published Y-STR profiles of the alleged 'Louis XVI blood' and 'Henri IV head' samples — inverting the earlier identifications of those relics. The paper is the canonical demonstration of why living-descendant Y-chromosomal data, not isolated historical samples, are the necessary anchor for any claim of identification across many generations. This is the exact logic underpinning the collaboration with Pieter van Vlaanderen: the question is not whether any single historical sample can be recovered, but whether the Y-profiles of multiple independently-documented living descendants of the project's hypothesised founders converge on a single ancestral signature.

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., Vanoverbeke, J., Gielis, G., Vanderheyden, N., Larmuseau, H.F.M., & Decorte, R.
entries.title: In the name of the migrant father — Analysis of surname origins identifies genetic admixture events undetectable from genealogical records
entries.note: Demonstrates that surname origin (as a proxy for ancestral geography) can resolve genetic admixture events invisible to in-depth pedigree genealogy alone. The case study is the 16th-century French-to-Flemish demic migration from Northern France into Dutch-speaking Flanders, which left a detectable genetic signal across the border region despite being largely undocumented in surviving civil and parish records. Method-relevant for any analysis of Van Vlaenderen cluster geography: concrete precedent for how a toponymic surname can carry genetic signal of historical migration events that genealogy alone cannot recover.

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., Boon, N., Vanderheyden, N., Van Geystelen, A., Larmuseau, H.F.M., Matthys, K., De Clercq, W., & Decorte, R.
entries.title: High Y-chromosomal diversity and low relatedness between paternal lineages on a communal scale in the Western European Low Countries during the surname establishment
entries.note: A Flanders-scale study of Y-chromosomal diversity across six Flemish communities at the time of surname establishment (13th–17th c.), finding high Y-chromosomal diversity and low within-community relatedness among citizens carrying distinct surnames. Directly relevant to the project's founder-count question: the baseline expectation for a generic toponymic surname in the Low Countries is that bearers within a single community should NOT share a recent common paternal ancestor. If a Flemish Y-DNA project of Van Vlaenderen bearers were to find substantially more within-name relatedness than Larmuseau's communal-scale baseline predicts, that would be positive evidence for a bastard-line or office-holder-founder model over a generic toponymic one.

entries.author: Larmuseau, M.H.D., et al.
entries.title: A Historical-Genetic Reconstruction of Human Extra-Pair Paternity
entries.publisher: Current Biology, 29 (2019), pp. 4102-4107.
entries.note: The De Patrijzen study. Confirms De Patrijzen concerns paternity certainty, not surname origins (the correct framing for the project's DNA page), and maps Larmuseau's lab infrastructure (DNA Brabant/Belgium, 1,638+ samples, Familiekunde Vlaanderen partnership since 2009). Source-noted. Received via Constance, June 2026.

entries.author: Nieus, Jean-François
entries.title: Aristocratic seal ownership in twelfth-century Flanders: A world in between
entries.publisher: Preprint. Academia.edu, 2021. University of Namur. Forthcoming in peer-reviewed publication.
entries.note: A sigillographic study of noble seal usage in the County of Flanders, 1071–1200. Establishes that territorial designations in the elite Flemish milieu functioned as political and dynastic language, not mere geographic labels. Documents Philip of Alsace placing the Flemish lion on the comital seal from 1163; confirms Michael II of Harnes (castellan of Cassel, constable of Flanders) as a Dover Recognitio sealer; and confirms the Praet lordship as an established noble entity from at least c.1190–1200. Provides contextual depth for the Van Vlaenderen surname hypothesis.
entries.availability: Full text on file with project. Note: this is a preprint; cite as forthcoming.

groups.heading: F. Late-Medieval Ghent Court Records and Post-1400 Prosopography

entries.author: De Vos, Tom
entries.title: Het overlevingsvermogen of bilevinghe als pasmunt bij scheiding en/of hertrouwen in het laatmiddeleeuwse Gent
entries.publisher: UGent Master's thesis, Faculteit Letteren en Wijsbegeerte, Vakgroep Middeleeuwen, Academiejaar 2007–2008. Promotor: Monique Vleeschouwers-Van Melkebeek; commissarissen: Thérèse de Hemptinne, Erik Thoen.
entries.note: The source that corrected the project's earlier 'Adam in Maldegem' misattribution. De Vos locates the 1447 Ghent partition case of Adam and Agnes sKokers (annulled marriage) in the Ghent schepenbank records, clarifying that the Adam figure belongs to the Ghent bilevinghe dossier rather than to a Maldegem context.

entries.author: Vleeschouwers-Van Melkebeek, Monique
entries.title: Eendrachtelic Commen ende Vriendelic Vereffent. Boedelverdelingen voor de Schepenen van de Keure van Gent tussen Echtparen Gescheiden van Tafel en Bed, 1439–1450
entries.publisher: Handelingen van de Koninklijke Commissie voor de Uitgave der Oude Wetten en Verordeningen van België, 47 (2006), 9–134.
entries.note: Edited collection of partition records from the Ghent Schepenen van de Keure, 1439–1450. Covers the period of the Adam–Agnes sKokers 1447 case reconstructed by De Vos (2008). The two editions together supply the documentary basis for the Ghent side of the Adam reattribution.

entries.author: Vleeschouwers-Van Melkebeek, Monique
entries.title: Daere nochtan den ghetrauden man niet emmer stonde te scheedene. Litigieuze boedelverdelingen voor de schepenen van de Keure van Gent. 1439–1450
entries.publisher: Handelingen der Maatschappij voor Geschiedenis en Oudheidkunde te Gent, 59 (2005), 117–133.
entries.note: Companion to the 2006 edition; covers contested partition cases from the same Ghent schepenbank corpus. Read alongside the 2006 volume for the full apparatus on annulled-marriage partitions in Ghent, 1439–1450.

entries.author: Valkeneers, Nina & Soen, Violet
entries.year: 2014 [based on N. Valkeneers's 2014 KU Leuven master's thesis; published article venue and year unconfirmed]
entries.title: Praet, Bronkhorst en Boetzelaer. Adellijke weduwes in de bres voor het calvinisme tijdens en na de Beeldenstorm (1566–1567)
entries.publisher: Belgian academic journal/proceedings article, pp. 265–284; the specific venue is not stated in the copy on file. Received directly from Prof. Violet Soen via academia.edu, April 2026.
entries.note: Documents the post-1545 Praet–Bronckhorst–Boetzelaer family network relevant to the later generations of the Van Vlaenderen-Praet line, including Jacob van Vlaanderen's 1552 marriage to Catharina van Boetzelaer and residence at the Vrijhof (Huys van Praet) at Aalter. Based on N. Valkeneers's unpublished KU Leuven master's thesis (2014); the published venue and year remain unconfirmed, so the date is carried per the project source note. Full citation to be finalised on the published version.

entries.author: Decavele, Johan
entries.title: Catharina van Boetzelaer, kasteelvrouwe van Aalter. Protestantisme volgens adellijk recept
entries.publisher: In: De eerste protestanten in de Lage Landen. Leuven, 2004. pp. 159–171.
entries.note: Essential source for the post-1545 Praet generation at Aalter. Page 166 specifically carries the 'geruïneerd' statement about Lodewijk V van Vlaenderen-Praet that anchors the project's account of the Aalter estate's decline. Acquisition in progress; when the scan arrives, the relevant PraetLineageDossier passages will be re-audited against the primary text.

entries.author: Huygens Instituut
entries.title: Catharina van Boetzelaer — Digitaal Vrouwenlexicon van Nederland
entries.publisher: Huygens ING, Digitaal Vrouwenlexicon van Nederland.
entries.note: The Huygens Institute's authoritative biographical entry for Catharina van Boetzelaer, identified in April 2026 as the key source resolving the post-1545 Van Vlaenderen-Praet generation. Read in conjunction with Decavele (2004) and Valkeneers & Soen (2015) for the full post-1545 prosopographical context.

entries.author: Van Vlaanderen, Pieter Antheunisz
entries.title: Stamreeks van Vlaanderen — De Zeeuwse Tak-2, ~1500 tot 2020
entries.publisher: Privately compiled family register. Author resident in Schoorl, The Netherlands.
entries.note: A private, collaborator-compiled register of the 'Zeeuwse Tak' (Zeeland branch) of the Van Vlaenderen family from approximately 1500 through 2020, prepared by Pieter Antheunisz van Vlaanderen in Schoorl. The register documents the Zeeland line descending from Laureys Arentsz van Vlaenderen, schoolmaster at Ritthem (attested 1588, d. late 1601), whose signature appears on the cover alongside the compiler's own. This compilation is the documentary basis for the ongoing Big Y-700 testing collaboration between Pieter and this project: the reconstructed Zeeland lineage serves as the reference pedigree against which Y-chromosomal results can be interpreted. Cited here to declare the provenance of the DNA collaboration transparently; as a privately-compiled family register, it is treated as a collaborator-provided secondary source rather than a peer-reviewed scholarly publication.

entries.author: Lichtervelde, P. de
entries.title: Les Bâtards de Louis de Male
entries.publisher: Handelingen van het Genootschap voor Geschiedenis 78(1-2) (1935), pp. 48–58.
entries.note: The standard early-twentieth-century census of Louis II de Male's natural children. Lichtervelde documents at least eighteen of Louis de Male's bastards — seven adult sons named in the 1384 testament plus eleven children at the Gosnay nursery establishment (ADN B 16228 N° 10948), framed as a floor rather than a total. Cites archival material at Brussels A.G.R., Lille A.D.N., and Dijon Côte d'Or. The load-bearing modern source for the comital-bastard cohort frame across the Phase 2 research findings; entry added in May 2026 as part of the Phase 2 site build.

entries.author: Donche, Pieter
entries.title: De Familie Van Drincham, gezegd van Vlaanderen (ca. 1350 tot 16de eeuw)
entries.publisher: Vlaamse Stam: tijdschrift voor familiegeschiedenis, jg. 42, nr. 6 (november 2006), pp. 548-580. Vlaamse Vereniging voor Familiekunde, Antwerp/Merksem.
entries.note: The canonical scholarly study of the Drincham line: the original Van Drincham nobles of Drincham parish (kasselrij Broekburg) and the new 'Van Drincham, gezegd van Vlaanderen' family descended from Jan 'sans terre' van Vlaenderen (d. Nicopolis 1396) through his marriage to Wilhelmine van Drincham. Reconstructed primarily from the leenregisters and leenverheffingsrekeningen of Veurne, Sint-Winnoksbergen, and Broekburg. Cited throughout the Drincham dossier, including the 1393 Broekburg relief (p. 556), the 1459 Veurne tomb (p. 573), and the 1466 Houtem tomb 'Mer Jans van Vlandres gheseit Drincham' (p. 567) used in the project's naming-convention and register analyses.

entries.author: Kusman, David
entries.title: Jean de Mirabello dit van Haelen (ca. 1280-1333). Haute finance et Lombards en Brabant
entries.publisher: Revue belge de philologie et d'histoire, 77/4 (1999), pp. 843-931.
entries.note: The modern scholarly study of the Mirabello (van Halen) family — the family into which the comital natural daughter Isabella van Lierde married. Corroborates the sister-reading ('Isabelle de Lierde, soeur bâtarde de Louis de Nevers, en 1324', p. 881) and the de Somerghem / Zomergem identity; the husband is Jean's son Simon (sgr. de Perwez), not Jean himself. Cross-flags the Three-Elisabeths disambiguation. Full PDF on file (Persée). Consulted 13 Jun 2026.

entries.author: Sabbe, J.
entries.title: De ondergang van twee Vlaamse adellijke geslachten in de 14e eeuw: de heren van Wessegem en van Praet
entries.publisher: Handelingen van het Genootschap voor Geschiedenis (Emulation Brugge / HvGG), vol. 103 (1966).
entries.note: Load-bearing for the Praet-line transition 1373–1379 and the Wessegem seigniorial extinction in 1363. Consulted 26 May 2026; source-noted.

entries.author: Carlier, Myriam
entries.title: Kinderen van de minne? Bastaarden in het 15de-eeuwse Vlaanderen
entries.publisher: Brussels: VUBPress, 2001. 328 pp.
entries.note: Thematic study of the social position of bastards in 15th-century Flanders (Ghent, Bruges, Kortrijk); a key framework source for the project's comital-bastard argument. A 2004 review is on file, but the book itself has not been read directly. Acquisition target.

entries.author: Decavele, Johan
entries.title: Katharina van Boetzelaer, een merkwaardig figuur in het protestants verzet tijdens het 'wonderjaar' (1566)
entries.publisher: Vereniging voor de geschiedenis van het Belgisch Protestantisme, vol. 5 (1969), pp. 151-171.
entries.note: Primary-source-grounded study of Catharina van Boetzelaer's Calvinist activities during the Wonderyear 1566, distinct from the 2004 Decavele chapter (decavele-2004) on the same subject in a different venue. Acquisition would upgrade the Calvinist-sympathies layer of the Van Vlaenderen-Praet terminal-generation narrative; not yet in hand.
